verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs confirm it keeps audit logs. Agent activity is attributed to service accounts so automated actions can be identified in audit logs, and audit logs can be monitored across a group in AI governance. The evidence covers only the AI-agent context, though, not a general log of user and administrative actions. Missing for 10: documentation of audit events for user and admin actions (e.g., permission changes, settings changes, logins), instance-level or admin audit log views, search, filter and export, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can review an audit log of user and administrative actions

citations.quote: Monitor AI agent sessions, audit logs, and developer exposure across a group.
All agent activities are clearly attributed to a service account, making it easy to identify automated actions in audit logs and commit histories.
